faqs.q: How Do I Find The Value Of My Gibson Acoustic Guitar Guitar?
faqs.a: Start with the exact model, then use its value guide to match the year, configuration and condition. The examples on this hub are selected references, not full-model ranges. I can begin an individual appraisal with clear photographs and the history you know.

faqs.q: Are All These Prices Based On The Same Condition?
faqs.a: No. Existing site anchors, published excellent-condition references and completed-sale comparison envelopes have different assumptions. The model guide identifies the condition and source basis. Don't apply a clean-original reference to a repaired or modified guitar without a separate assessment.

faqs.q: Does Every Annual Row Represent Separate Sales?
faqs.a: No. Where evidence supports an era rather than individual years, the model guide labels the shared band and repeats it for each covered year. A row helps locate the year; it doesn't imply an independent same-year sales sample.

faqs.q: Can I Use A Current Listing As A Completed Price?
faqs.a: No. An advertised amount is an asking price. A sold label doesn't always disclose the final negotiated amount either. I keep realized transactions, published references and asking references identified separately.

faqs.q: Does A Quality Refret Remove All-Original Status?
faqs.a: Under this site's grading approach, a quality refret preserves the all-original classification of an otherwise original instrument while removing museum-quality status. Refinishing, neck reshaping and structural repairs are separate changes.
No. The references help organize an appraisal. A purchase offer depends on the actual instrument and sale terms, and an owner's net proceeds may differ from a retail transaction total.
